title: [27/2/2024] Percentage of UK residents interested in named sports
prompt: The table below shows the results of surveys of people in the UK, carried out in three different decades. It shows the percentages of people who said they were interested in certain sports. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make a comparison where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The table illustrates the percentage of UK residents who expressed interest in six different sports over three decades, from 1990 to 2010.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, football, golf, and judo experienced declining popularity over the given period, while interest in rugby, cricket, and swimming showed an upward trend. Throughout the two decades, football consistently remained the most popular sport, attracting more than half of the population.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding sports with declining interest, football led this group with 59% of people showing interest in 1990, which was significantly higher than golf at 28% and judo at 9%. Football's popularity gradually decreased over the next two decades, falling by 3 percent to 56% by 2010. Similarly, golf maintained stable figures until 2000 before declining slightly to 26% in the final year. Judo experienced the most dramatic fall, with interest more than halving from 9% to just 4% over the twenty-year period.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for sports gaining popularity, in 1990 swimming attracted 15% of the population, slightly higher than both rugby and cricket which stood at 12%. Rugby showed the most substantial growth, doubling its percentage to 24% by 2010, while cricket saw a modest increase to 14% by the end of the period. Swimming also demonstrated an overall positive trend, rising from 15% to 18% in 2000, though it slightly declined to 16% in the final year.
